reason: Reproduced by driving the master, not by reading. render-b.js:688 stores focus:function(){event.currentTarget.focus({preventScroll:true})} on the step() undo entry; the closure reads event.currentTarget after dispatch has ended, when Chromium has nulled it. With a pageerror listener attached before driving, clicking .b-step[aria-label="Move a week earlier"] then pressing Undo fires exactly one "Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading focus)" per press at 390, 768, 1152, 1279, 1280 and 1440 — and on BOTH paths, the clicked .b-undoAct and Ctrl+Z, which the finding treats as possibly different. Zero errors fire on the step itself; the throw is purely the undo. The throw lands at 'if (top.focus) top.focus();' (render-b.js:540), one line above 'if (typeof top.at === "number") window.scrollTo(0, top.at);' (541), so the place restore never runs. Measured with .b-measureHead top, scrolling 700px away between the move and the press: 1440 goes 251 → -449 and stays at -449 after Undo (700px adrift); 1280 identical. Two further consequences the finding is right about and the gates do not see: on the clicked-Undo path activeElement after Undo is .b-edit, not the .b-step that made the change — the stated focus promise is broken outright on the path an owner using the mouse takes; and interaction-check.mjs asserts 'undo returns focus to the control that made the change' (line 468) only on the Ctrl+Z path, where focus was already sitting on the .b-step, so the exception aborting the handler cannot fail it. Not a restatement of the gates: 'zero console errors across all states' is evaluated at interaction-check.mjs:77, before any interactive block runs, and pageErrors is never read again; the only scroll-restore assertion, 'the way back returns the view' (1340), presses delete, whose entry carries no focus closure and therefore does not throw. Not already handled: there is no try/catch anywhere on that call. Not taste, not a constraint breach, and the fix touches no colour, weight or architecture. One correction: at 390/768/1152/1279 the view DOES come back to the pixel despite the throw — the editor's own keepInBand/place work inside top.undo() happens to land it there, not window.scrollTo — so the finding's '219 to -285 at 390' is wrong. The defect stands at the two widths the finding measured hardest, and the uncaught TypeError itself stands at all six.
sharpenedFix: In step(), capture the node before the closure: as the first line of the click handler add 'var pressed = event.currentTarget;' and store 'focus: function () { pressed.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }'. That alone removes the throw and restores both promises. Then harden undo() so no future closure can eat the place restore: move 'if (typeof top.at === "number") window.scrollTo(0, top.at);' above the focus call and wrap the focus call in try/catch. Note the ordering nuance the finding misses — restoring scroll BEFORE focus is only safe because every focus call here passes preventScroll:true; keep that flag or the restore is undone by the browser's own scroll-into-view. For the gate, two additions, and put the second one where it actually bites: in the reversibility block, after a .b-step move, scrollBy(0,700), press .b-undoAct, and require .b-measureHead to return within 2px, run at 1280 and 1440 where the current delete-only test would not have caught this; and assert on the clicked-Undo path (not just Ctrl+Z) that activeElement is the .b-step. Separately, move the pageErrors assertion from line 77 to the end of the run so it covers the whole interactive suite rather than load only — it is a one-line move and it is what would have caught this in round 6.
